**Proposed mechanism:** Translocation events (e.g., PAX3-FOXO1 fusion) —DISRUPTS→ PAX3 (HGNC:7819); Translocation events (e.g., PAX3-FOXO1 fusion) —DISRUPTS→ FOXO1 (HGNC:3744); PAX3 (HGNC:7819) —DISRUPTS→ Skeletal muscle differentiation program (GO:0030198); FOXO1 (HGNC:3744) —DISRUPTS→ Skeletal muscle differentiation program (GO:0030198); Skeletal muscle differentiation program (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma (MONDO:0009994); Loss-of-function mutations in PAX3/PAX7 —DISRUPTS→ PAX7 (HGNC:7821); PAX3 (HGNC:7819) —DISRUPTS→ Neural development program (GO:0048666); PAX7 (HGNC:7821) —DISRUPTS→ Neural development program (GO:0048666); Neural development program (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ Karayayol-Borroto-Haghshenas neurodevelopmental syndrome (MONDO:0975836). Aberrant transcription factor activity arising from translocations involving PAX3 and FOXO1 (n8->n1, n8->n3) disrupts skeletal muscle differentiation (n1->n4, n3->n4), leading to alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma (n4->n6). The shared disruption of developmental programs by PAX family members and FOXO1 forms the mechanistic link.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of mutations or translocations in PAX3, PAX7, or FOXO1 in patients diagnosed with either alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma or Karayayol-Borroto-Haghshenas neurodevelopmental syndrome, or if these variants are found at high frequency (>5%) in the general population via gnomAD, would challenge this hypothesis. _(variant: PAX3, PAX7, FOXO1 variants)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared regulatory pathways involving PAX3, PAX7, and FOXO1 could reveal common therapeutic targets for both pediatric cancers and neurodevelopmental disorders, potentially leading to novel treatment strategies that address the underlying molecular etiology.
